meaning: Computing the image a camera would see of a scene that exists only as numbers.
A surface stored as a set of triangles; how a simulator holds every shape it draws.
Making an image by projecting each triangle onto it and filling the pixels the triangle covers.
Making an image by following a ray from the camera through each pixel to the surface it lands on, then more rays from that point.
A ray sent from a point on a surface toward a light; if something blocks it, the point is in shadow.
A tree of nested boxes around the triangles of a scene; a ray tracer walks it to find which triangle a ray lands on first.
A unit on some NVIDIA GPUs built to speed up the BVH walk of ray tracing; data-centre training GPUs such as the H100 lack it.
The units of an NVIDIA GPU that multiply matrices, the arithmetic of training and running a neural network.
The units of a GPU that run ordinary GPU code, such as batched physics or a ray tracer written as code.
The fixed-function engine on a GPU that compresses frames into video.
The fixed-function engine on a GPU that turns video back into frames.
The video codec LeRobot writes by default; some data-centre GPUs cannot decode it in hardware.
NVIDIA's name for rendering that hands the ray search to the RT cores; the renderer of Isaac Sim works this way.
Running a simulator with neither camera images nor an interactive view; Isaac Lab 3.0's install guide adds a renderer's requirements only when one of them is needed.
One simulated copy of the scene plus its task; training runs thousands side by side on a GPU.
A small standard control task, a cart balancing a pole, used in Isaac Lab's benchmark.
Drawing every environment's camera into one tile of a single large GPU image in one pass, then cutting it apart into a tensor the policy reads on the GPU.
NVIDIA's simulator application; it renders with RTX and requires a GPU with RT cores.
NVIDIA's robot-learning framework; since version 3.0 it runs without Isaac Sim.
EC2 GPU instance families: G carries GPUs with RT cores, P carries data-centre training GPUs.
Light that reaches a surface straight from a lamp, with no bounce off other surfaces; all that Isaac Lab's Newton Warp renderer computes.
NVIDIA's Python framework for writing GPU code; MuJoCo Warp and the Newton Warp renderer are built on it.
The RTX renderer that Isaac Lab 3.0's documentation recommends; it runs without Isaac Sim and needs RT cores.
MuJoCo's word for one independent copy of the scene in a batch; Isaac Lab counts environments.
Varying the simulator's rendering and physics so widely during training that the real scene falls inside the range.
The 64-bit Arm processor architecture, used by AWS Graviton and the NVIDIA DGX Spark.
The trained model that reads the robot's observation, here camera images and joint angles, and decides what the motors do next.
A GPU physics engine built on Warp that Isaac Lab 3.0 runs its tasks on; it can run headless with no RTX hardware.
The GPU version of the MuJoCo physics engine, written in Warp; it steps thousands of worlds at once and ships a batch ray tracer for cameras.
NVIDIA's ray-tracing library for RTX GPUs; MuJoCo Warp's optional hardware back end is built on it and falls back to the Warp path when it is unavailable.
The throughput figure in Isaac Lab's benchmark: the rate of simulated frames a training run gets through, with the policy's updates included.
The Isaac Lab paper's highest-fidelity camera type; it runs out of memory beyond 48 cameras on a 96 GB card.
Isaac Lab's camera sensor class that draws every environment's camera in one tiled pass; it scales to several thousand environments.
Isaac Lab's camera that casts its rays with Warp; faster than the tiled camera at low resolutions, by the Isaac Lab paper.
DeepMind's open-source physics simulator; its built-in renderers rasterise and need no RT cores.
DeepMind's suite of ready-made robot tasks on MuJoCo, including the SO-101 pick-cube task that renders a 64x64 wrist image.
The physics engine inside Isaac Sim; Isaac Lab 3.0 can run its tasks on it or on Newton.
The part of a training process that updates the policy; Isaac Lab's memory figures include it.
An EC2 reservation type that, unlike Capacity Blocks, covers G instances.
An EC2 reservation of a block of GPU instances for a fixed window; the list read on 2026-11-20 holds P and Trainium types and no G type.
